findings: Portfolio is three frozen-anchor cells plus one diagnostic, not a model leaderboard: (A) HANNA overlap repair, (B) expert-edit ranking, (C) non-overlapping HBQ benefit, (D) optional cheap judge-stability check. Ship gates use A+B; C is a separate claim; D never decides product.

Cell A (overlap-focused repair): score only rubric dimensions with predeclared construct overlap to HANNA (overall quality, coherence, interestingness or equivalent). Metric is held-out Spearman/Kendall plus pairwise ranking accuracy against HANNA human scores. Purpose is calibration and wording repair of the overlapping slice. Non-overlapping HBQ items are excluded from this cell so HANNA cannot launder new benefits.

Cell B (expert-edit preference): each item is a draft vs an expert human revision. The product test is directional: the frozen rubric judge must rank the expert edit higher on the dimensions the edit was intended to improve, with a pre-registered minimum win-rate and a no-regression check on untouched dimensions. This is a preference probe, not a cardinal quality lab.

Cell C (non-overlapping HBQ benefits): evaluate only HBQ items with no HANNA construct overlap, and only on expert-edit pairs whose revision notes target those benefits. Do not correlate these items with HANNA overall. Optional negative control: non-overlap HBQ should not be required to track HANNA; if it does, treat that as leakage, not success.

Held-outs are by artifact, not by prompt tweak: freeze HANNA story IDs and expert-edit pair IDs used for rubric wording, few-shots, weights, or thresholds. Official numbers come only from the unused remainder. If N is tight, use a single pre-registered confirmation split rather than nested CV theater.

Trusted-judge policy is cell-specific, not every-model: Cell A may use one frozen high-stability judge chosen for rank correlation with HANNA humans. Cell B may use a different frozen judge if pairwise preference is more robust than absolute scoring. Cell C must use the production rubric judge (the shipped artifact). Development models may iterate on the train split only; they do not fill official cells.

Sparsity rules: one official judge per cell, one confirmation split, a short dimension allow-list, and no extra datasets, style proxies, or automatic-metric zoo. Cross-judge agreement is a diagnostic on a small shared subset, not a full judge × model × dimension matrix.
recommendations: Pre-register a construct map: each rubric/HBQ item is tagged overlap-with-HANNA, expert-edit-only, or out-of-scope. Overlap items may be repaired on Cell A; only non-overlap items may claim HBQ benefit on Cell C.

Lock artifacts before scoring: HANNA ratings, expert revision pairs, judge IDs, prompts, and aggregation rules. Re-run official cells only when the rubric or production judge changes; do not refresh because a new model is convenient.

Report Cell A as repair (did overlapping ranks get closer to HANNA humans?) and Cell C as incremental benefit (did non-overlapping HBQ move expert-edit ranking where the edit targeted that benefit?). Never pool them into one alignment score.

Use win-rate with Wilson or bootstrap intervals on Cell B, plus a small error taxonomy (edit wins on target dimension, edit wins for the wrong reason, original preferred, tie). Cardinal score gaps are secondary.

Keep product gates tiny: ship if held-out Cell A rank agreement meets the pre-set floor and Cell B expert-edit win-rate meets the pre-set floor with no severe untouched-dimension regression. Treat Cell C as a benefit appendix, not a blocker, until overlap leakage is ruled out.
If a cell is underpowered, shrink the claim rather than add datasets or fresh humans: fewer dimensions, a directional test, or 'insufficient evidence' on that slice.
risks: Overlap contamination: scoring non-overlapping HBQ items against HANNA overall, or folding Cell A and Cell C into one number, will fake human alignment and hide whether new benefits are real.
Held-out leakage via rubric prose, examples, or thresholds tuned on the same HANNA stories or revision pairs later reported as confirmation.
Judge shopping and self-preference: running every model through every cell, or using a generator-family judge on its own drafts, inflates alignment without a frozen trusted judge.
Expert edits that fix off-rubric issues (false misses) or that humans like for reasons HANNA would not reward (false hits); without revision-intent labels, Cell B overclaims.
Small-N, genre, and length shift: HANNA and the revision set may not match product traffic, so a passing gate can still fail in-product on other forms.
Treating this portfolio as a benchmark lab (extra models, extra metrics, leaderboards) burns the sparse human anchors and turns product evidence into irreproducible bakeoff noise.
output.summary: A sparse product gate, not a lab: repair overlapping rubric dimensions on held-out HANNA rankings, test whether a frozen judge ranks expert edits higher, and claim non-overlapping HBQ benefits only on intent-matched edits—never via HANNA. One trusted judge per cell, production judge required for HBQ, development models stay off official numbers.
